input: Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

red_flags.claim: Financial-crime controls: the Bank of Lithuania fined group entity Revolut Bank UAB €3.5 million for AML/CTF violations.
Consumer-treatment risk: Italy's competition authority imposed fines involving Revolut Group Holdings Ltd over investment disclosures, account restrictions and Italian-IBAN information.
Data-disclosure controls failed: Revolut confirmed releasing sensitive customer information in response to fraudulent government-domain requests; the exact affected-customer count was not disclosed.
Product-governance scrutiny: press reporting described a PRA section 166 review of product-approval controls. This is a reported review, not a published finding of wrongdoing.

traction.claim: Company claim: year-end retail customers reached 68.3 million, up 30% year on year; business customers reached 767,000, up 33%.
Company claim: an undated page observed on this date lists 75 million-plus personal customers and 800,000-plus business customers globally; these are customer counts, not verified active-user counts.
Company claim: the customer-stories page names Deel, Rakuten France, Lyca Mobile and Aer Lingus among users of its business or payment services; individual relationship dates are not supplied.
Company claim: Booking.com adopted Revolut Pay for customer checkout and Revolut Business to support the payment solution.

missing_fields: funding: completion, transaction size, buyers and any new-capital component of the July 2026 employee share-sale process were not verified.
financial_signals: FY2026 interim financial results, current group headcount and any current group-wide layoff programme were not verified.
team: continuation of Victor Stinga as CFO after the March 2026 annual-report snapshot was not verified.
legal_and_regulatory: current sanctions-list exposure was not independently verified; no conclusion of 'no sanctions exposure' is supported.
legal_and_regulatory: exact affected-customer counts and final regulatory outcomes for the September 2026 data incidents were not verified.
legal_and_regulatory: the final order, costs and subsequent appeals in the PSR litigation were not verified.
reputation: the direction of the overall employee-rating trend was not established from the opened review page.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: The Bank of Lithuania's register records a €3.5 million fine against Revolut Bank UAB for breaches of AML/CTF requirements; the sanctioned entity is the group's Lithuanian bank.

Revolut Bank UAB was a claimant in judicial-review proceedings against the Payment Systems Regulator. The High Court held that the PSR had statutory power to cap cross-border interchange fees; this was not enforcement litigation against Revolut.

Revolut announced that the PRA lifted mobilisation restrictions on Revolut Bank UK Ltd, enabling its bank launch and eligible FSCS-protected deposits. Customer onboarding and migration were to be phased.

AGCM fined Revolut Group Holdings Ltd with Revolut Securities Europe UAB €5 million over investment disclosures, and with Revolut Bank UAB €5 million over account restrictions plus €1.5 million over Italian-IBAN information.

Revolut confirmed disclosing sensitive customer data, including identity-document copies, after fraudulent requests from a legitimate government-agency domain. It said affected customers and relevant authorities were notified; the exact customer count was undisclosed.

RTÉ reported a separate exposure of historical Revolut customer records at brokerage provider DriveWealth. Revolut said its own systems were not compromised and customer funds and investments were safe.

PYMNTS, citing Financial Times reporting, said the PRA commissioned a section 166 review around the UK bank's launch to examine product-approval controls. Revolut and the Bank of England declined comment; no final finding was reported.

reputation.claim: Review-aggregator snapshot observed on this date: Glassdoor displayed 4.3/5 from 6,609 reviews and 84% recommending Revolut. These are anonymous, self-selected employee reviews, not a representative workforce survey.

Glassdoor themes include autonomy and strong colleagues alongside aggressive targets, burnout risk and poor work-life balance. The opened page did not establish a direction for the overall rating trend.

Company-reported complaint pattern: the Italian branch of Revolut Bank UAB recorded 1,992 complaints during 2025, including 513 concerning attempted payment fraud and 433 concerning account opening or restrictions. These are branch-level figures, not group totals.

output.verdict: Strong customer growth, diversified revenues and audited profitability support Revolut's commercial strength. Investment work should focus on financial-crime and product controls, consumer-treatment remediation and data security, while independently establishing the terms and completion of its latest secondary sale.

financial_signals.claim: FY2025 audited group revenue was £4,515.770 million, profit before tax £1,713.273 million and net profit £1,304.628 million. The company reported revenue growth of 46% and pre-tax profit growth of 57% versus FY2024.
Company-reported total customer balances reached £50.2 billion at year-end 2025, up 66% year on year. This is the report's customer-balances measure, not solely bank deposits.
Group year-end employees increased to 12,200 from 10,133 at year-end 2024; annual-average employees were 10,909 versus 9,932. These measures should not be mixed.
BDO LLP's audit opinion on the FY2025 financial statements states that they give a true and fair view.
Company hiring plan disclosed in the annual report: up to 800 employees in Spain by 2028. This is a forward-looking plan, not completed hiring.

team.claim: The official leadership page lists Nik Storonsky as co-founder and CEO; he launched Revolut in 2015 and previously traded equity derivatives at Credit Suisse and Lehman Brothers.
The official page lists co-founder Vlad Yatsenko as a non-executive board member; his prior experience includes financial-software work at UBS and Deutsche Bank.

Notable operational departure: Bloomberg reported Yatsenko would step down as CTO in July 2026, with Donato Lucia succeeding him as VP of Technology and Yatsenko transitioning to a non-executive board role.
The official page lists Martin Gilbert as chair; he previously co-founded and led Aberdeen Asset Management. Donato Lucia is listed as VP of Technology.
The annual-report leadership snapshot identifies Victor Stinga as CFO. His continuation in that role as of November 2026 was not separately verified.
Revolut announced Chief Banking Officer Sid Jajodia's appointment as a group executive director, subject to regulatory approvals. His prior employers include PayU, LendingClub and Capital One.

business.claim: Revolut serves individuals and businesses with spending, payments, saving, investing, borrowing and business-finance services.
The company website lists a free Standard consumer plan and paid Premium and Metal subscriptions; this is an observed product-menu snapshot.
FY2025 revenue streams included card payments, interest income, subscriptions, wealth and foreign exchange; fee-based revenue represented 76% of turnover.

The London-headquartered group reported serving customers across 39 countries at December 2025 and operating as a licensed bank in 30 countries. Operating markets should not be confused with supported transfer destinations.

funding.claim: Revolut announced a $250 million Series C at a $1.7 billion valuation, led by DST Global.
Revolut closed its Series D at $580 million, including an $80 million extension from TSG Consumer Partners.
Revolut raised $800 million at a $33 billion valuation in July 2021; TechCrunch identified SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Tiger Global as Series E co-leads.

Company-confirmed completed share sale established a $75 billion valuation and provided employee liquidity. Coatue, Greenoaks, Dragoneer and Fidelity Management & Research Company led the transaction; its size was not disclosed in the opened announcement.
Bloomberg reported an employee secondary-sale process at a $115 billion valuation. This establishes an announced process and valuation, not verified completion or fresh capital raised by Revolut.

Trade-press indication observed on this date: FinanceFeeds reported secondary-market pricing implying approximately $125 billion. It explicitly distinguished this from a newly announced funding-round valuation; it is not a verified completed company financing.

citations.title: AGCM - The Italian Competition Authority fines Revolut over €11 million for unfair commercial practices
excerpts: The Italian Competition Authority has fined Revolut Securities Europe UAB, a company of the group which offers investment services in Europe, and Revolut Group Holdings Ltd over 11 million euro for engaging in unfair commercial practices. Specifically, the two companies were fined 5 million euro for breaching articles 20, 21 and 22 of the Consumer Code: they failed to clearly disclose, from the very first point of contact with clients, the additional costs and limitations involved in commission-free investments. These investments include fractional shares, which – when compared to full shares – involve significant differences, also in terms of risks, rights and transferability of shares. The Authority also imposed a fine totalling 5 million euro on Revolut Group Holdings Ltd and Revolut Bank UAB, a company of the group offering banking services in Europe. It found that the companies had used aggressive practices in managing the suspension, limitation and blocking of payment accounts, while omitting (or failing to clearly provide) key information on the relevant terms and procedures. In particular, the companies did not provide clients with sufficient pre-contractual information, or advance notice before restrictions were imposed, nor did they provide an opportunity to respond or adequate assistance once restrictions had been imposed. Preventing users, sometimes for extended periods, from accessing funds and related services hinders their ability to exercise their contractual rights and meet everyday needs, including urgent ones. The Authority therefore found the conducts to be in breach of articles 20, 21, 22, 24 and 25 of the Consumer Code, in view of their potential to unduly influence the freedom of choice of consumers and microenterprises. Lastly, the Authority imposed a further 1.5 million euro fine on Revolut Group Holdings Ltd and Revolut Bank UAB for not providing clear and exhaustive information on the requirements and timeframe for obtaining an Italian IBAN (starting with IT) instead of a Lithuanian IBAN (starting with LT), in breach of articles 20, 21 and 22 of the Consumer Code. _Rome, 2 April 2026

citations.title: Revolut confirms customer data breach through fake government requests | TechCrunch
excerpts: British fintech Revolut confirmed that it disclosed sensitive customer information to an unauthorized third party after receiving fraudulent requests sent from a legitimate government agency email domain. The exposed data included customers’ identity and contact details, including their birth date, postal and email addresses, and phone numbers, as well as copies of their identity documents including passports and driver’s licenses, according to a notification emailed to affected customers and reviewed by TechCrunch. The data may have also included verification selfies, account statements, and transaction histories, the firm said in its notification. A Revolut spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch that a “limited” number of customers were impacted and said the company had contacted those customers directly. Revolut, however, did not disclose the exact number of impacted individuals. It also did not answer whether the incident was limited to a specific

basis.reasoning: The article reports company confirmation of disclosure and expressly notes the undisclosed customer count.

citations.title: PYMNTS | Revolut’s Product Approvals Face UK Regulatory Scrutiny
excerpts: The [Bank of England’s](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/) [Prudential Regulation Authority](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/what-is-the-prudential-regulation-authority-pra) (PRA) issued what is known as a section 166 earlier this year to investigate risks surrounding the speed of Revolut’s product launches, the Financial Times (FT) [reported](https://www.ft.com/content/ea6d6d50-57c0-4b21-a05f-df5efe020c24?syn-25a6b1a6=1) Tuesday (Oct. 27). The report, citing sources familiar with the matter, said the order was made around the time Revolut obtained its long-awaited full banking license in March and is designed to test the strength of the FinTech’s internal systems. As the FT notes, Revolut has amassed a customer base of more than 80 million in a little more than a decade, and is [valued at $115 billion](https://www.pymnts.com/news/investment-tracker/ipo/2026/revolut-chief-says-fintech-could-go-public-in-ny-and-london/) . With a section 166, a company is required to appoint advisors to examine its systems and controls, the report added. Typically this process involves an investigation by accountants and lawyers who will suggest improvements where necessary. If the review uncovers failures, the company could face penalties or enforcement actions.
